title: Leviticus Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Leviticus chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Leviticus Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Leviticus Chapter 7.

questions.question: What kind of offering is described as "most holy" in Leviticus 7?
options: Trespass offering
Burnt offering
Peace offering
Sin offering
questions.correctAnswer: Trespass offering
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:1 states that the law of the trespass offering is most holy.

questions.question: Where shall the trespass offering be killed according to Leviticus 7?
options: In the holy place
In the place where they kill the burnt offering
At the entrance of the tabernacle
In the camp
questions.correctAnswer: In the place where they kill the burnt offering
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:2 says the trespass offering shall be killed in the place where they kill the burnt offering.

questions.question: Which parts of the trespass offering are to be offered by fire upon the altar?
options: The rump, fat covering the inward parts, kidneys, and caul above the liver
Only the kidneys and rump
The whole animal except the hide
The head and the hooves
questions.correctAnswer: The rump, fat covering the inward parts, kidneys, and caul above the liver
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:3-4 details these specific parts to be offered by fire on the altar.

questions.question: Who is allowed to eat of the trespass offering, and where must it be eaten?
options: Every male among the priests, in the holy place
All Israelites, in their homes
Only the high priest, outside the camp
The family of the offerer, in the tabernacle court
questions.correctAnswer: Every male among the priests, in the holy place
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:6 states that every male priest shall eat of it in the holy place.

questions.question: True or False: The priest who offers a burnt offering shall keep the skin of the burnt offering for himself.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:8 says the priest who offers a burnt offering shall have the skin of that burnt offering.

questions.question: What kind of meat offerings are given to the priest who offers them?
options: Only those baked in the oven
Those baked in the oven and those dressed in the fryingpan and pan
Only dry meat offerings
Only meat offerings made without oil
questions.correctAnswer: Those baked in the oven and those dressed in the fryingpan and pan
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:9 states that all meat offerings baked in the oven or dressed in fryingpan or pan belong to the priest who offers them.

questions.question: How are meat offerings mingled with oil distributed among the sons of Aaron?
options: The oldest son gets the largest portion
They share equally, one as much as another
The high priest gets all
They are offered entirely on the altar
questions.correctAnswer: They share equally, one as much as another
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:10 says that every meat offering mingled with oil and dry is shared equally among the sons of Aaron.

questions.question: True or False: The law of the sacrifice of peace offerings is introduced in Leviticus 7 after the laws of trespass offerings.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:11 introduces the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings following the trespass offering laws.

questions.question: What must be offered along with a sacrifice of thanksgiving according to Leviticus 7?
options: Unleavened cakes mingled with oil, unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and cakes mingled with oil of fine flour, fried
Only unleavened bread
Leavened bread without oil
No bread or cakes are to be offered
questions.correctAnswer: Unleavened cakes mingled with oil, unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and cakes mingled with oil of fine flour, fried
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:12 details these items as offerings with a sacrifice of thanksgiving.

questions.question: Besides unleavened cakes, what else is offered with the sacrifice of thanksgiving of peace offerings?
options: Leavened bread
Only fruits
Only wine
No other offering is mentioned
questions.correctAnswer: Leavened bread
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:13 states that leavened bread is also offered with the sacrifice of thanksgiving of peace offerings.

questions.question: True or False: The flesh of a peace offering for thanksgiving shall be eaten the day it is offered and may be left until morning.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:15 says the flesh of the peace offering for thanksgiving shall be eaten the same day and not left until the morning.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 7, what happens to the remainder of a peace offering's flesh on the third day?
options: It shall be burnt with fire
It can be eaten freely
It is given to the poor
It is buried in the camp
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be burnt with fire
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:17 states that the remainder of the flesh on the third day must be burnt with fire.

questions.question: True or False: Eating the flesh of a peace offering on the third day is acceptable and will be imputed to the offerer.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:18 explains that eating the flesh on the third day is an abomination and will not be accepted or imputed to the offerer.

questions.question: Which comes first in Leviticus 7: the instruction about the trespass offering or the law concerning the skin of the burnt offering?
options: Instruction about the trespass offering
Law concerning the skin of the burnt offering
Law about peace offerings
Law about meat offerings
questions.correctAnswer: Instruction about the trespass offering
questions.explanation: The chapter starts with the law of the trespass offering (verse 1) before mentioning the skin of the burnt offering in verse 8.

questions.question: Who shall eat the meat offering mingled with oil and dry, according to Leviticus 7?
options: All the sons of Aaron equally
Only the high priest
The offerer and his family
The entire congregation
questions.correctAnswer: All the sons of Aaron equally
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:10 states all the sons of Aaron shall have the meat offering mingled with oil and dry equally.

medium.title: Leviticus Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Leviticus Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 7:14, what portion of the peace offering is given to the priest who sprinkles the blood?
options: One out of the whole oblation as a heave offering
The entire breast of the offering
The rump and kidneys
The right shoulder only
questions.correctAnswer: One out of the whole oblation as a heave offering
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:14 states that one out of the whole oblation shall be offered as a heave offering to the LORD and it shall be the priest's who sprinkles the blood of the peace offerings. This is distinct from the breast and right shoulder portions given elsewhere (verses 30-32).

questions.question: What instruction does Leviticus 7:15 give regarding the timing of eating the flesh of peace offerings for thanksgiving?
options: It must be eaten the same day and not left until morning
It can be eaten anytime within three days
It should be eaten the next day only
It should be burned if not eaten immediately
questions.correctAnswer: It must be eaten the same day and not left until morning
questions.explanation: Verse 15 commands that the flesh of peace offerings for thanksgiving be eaten the same day it is offered and not left until the morning, emphasizing prompt consumption (Leviticus 7:15).

questions.question: How long may the flesh of a vow or voluntary peace offering be eaten according to Leviticus 7:16?
options: The same day and the next day
Only the same day
Up to three days
Only the next day
questions.correctAnswer: The same day and the next day
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:16 explains that if the offering is a vow or voluntary, it shall be eaten the same day it is offered and also on the morrow, the next day.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 7:17 say should happen to the remainder of the flesh of the peace offering on the third day?
options: It shall be burnt with fire
It shall be eaten by the priests
It shall be given to the poor
It shall be offered again
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be burnt with fire
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that leftover flesh on the third day must be burnt with fire, emphasizing the importance of proper timing in consumption (Leviticus 7:17).

questions.question: What consequence does Leviticus 7:18 describe for anyone who eats the flesh of a peace offering on the third day?
options: The offering will not be accepted and the eater bears iniquity
They must offer another sacrifice
They are forgiven if they repent
They will be blessed
questions.correctAnswer: The offering will not be accepted and the eater bears iniquity
questions.explanation: Verse 18 states that eating the flesh on the third day is an abomination, and it will not be accepted nor imputed to the offerer; the person who eats it bears their iniquity.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 7:19, what happens to the flesh of the peace offering if it touches anything unclean?
options: It shall not be eaten and must be burnt with fire
It can be eaten if washed first
It must be given to the priests
It should be buried
questions.correctAnswer: It shall not be eaten and must be burnt with fire
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:19 instructs that any flesh touching an unclean thing must not be eaten but burnt with fire, showing the importance of ritual cleanliness.

questions.question: What penalty does Leviticus 7:20 prescribe for a person who eats the flesh of peace offerings while having uncleanness on them?
options: They shall be cut off from their people
They must bring a sin offering
They shall be forgiven after confession
They must offer a burnt offering
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be cut off from their people
questions.explanation: Verse 20 clearly states that the soul that eats the flesh of peace offerings with uncleanness upon them shall be cut off from their people, indicating a severe penalty for disobedience.

questions.question: Leviticus 7:21 outlines a penalty for touching any unclean thing and then eating the flesh of peace offerings. What is the penalty?
options: Cut off from his people
Must offer a burnt offering
Excommunication for seven days
No penalty if cleansed later
questions.correctAnswer: Cut off from his people
questions.explanation: This verse reiterates that anyone who touches unclean things and eats the peace offering flesh shall be cut off from their people, emphasizing strict holiness requirements.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 7:23 instruct concerning the eating of fat from ox, sheep, or goat?
options: Ye shall eat no manner of fat from these animals
You may eat fat from these animals only if sacrificed
Fat must be burned before eating
Fat can be eaten only by priests
questions.correctAnswer: Ye shall eat no manner of fat from these animals
questions.explanation: Verse 23 plainly commands the children of Israel not to eat any fat of ox, sheep, or goat, highlighting a specific dietary restriction.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 7:24, what may be done with the fat of beasts that die naturally or are torn by beasts?
options: It may be used for any other use but not eaten
It must be burnt immediately
It may be eaten if cooked thoroughly
It must be given to the priests
questions.correctAnswer: It may be used for any other use but not eaten
questions.explanation: Verse 24 clarifies that fat from beasts that die of themselves or are torn may be used for other purposes but must not be eaten, distinguishing use from consumption.

questions.question: What consequence does Leviticus 7:25 say will come to anyone who eats the fat of the beasts used in offerings made by fire unto the LORD?
options: That soul shall be cut off from his people
They shall bring a sin offering
They must fast for seven days
They shall be forgiven upon confession
questions.correctAnswer: That soul shall be cut off from his people
questions.explanation: Verse 25 states that anyone who eats such fat will be cut off from his people, emphasizing the seriousness of the prohibition.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 7:26 forbid concerning blood?
options: You shall eat no manner of blood of fowl or beast in your dwellings
You may drink blood if it is from a clean animal
Blood may be used only for offerings
Blood can be eaten only by priests
questions.correctAnswer: You shall eat no manner of blood of fowl or beast in your dwellings
questions.explanation: Verse 26 forbids eating any blood of bird or beast within the dwellings, underscoring a strict dietary law.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 7:18, eating the flesh of peace offerings on the third day is acceptable if the person repents immediately.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:18 clearly states that eating the flesh on the third day is an abomination and will not be accepted, and the eater bears their iniquity, with no mention of repentance changing this outcome.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 7:20 teaches that a person who eats peace offering flesh with uncleanness upon them will be cut off from their people.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 20 explicitly states that the soul who eats the flesh of peace offerings with uncleanness upon them shall be cut off from their people, indicating a serious consequence.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 7:27 say will happen to anyone who eats any manner of blood?
options: That soul shall be cut off from his people
They shall be cleansed by water
They must offer a burnt offering
They will be forgiven if they confess
questions.correctAnswer: That soul shall be cut off from his people
questions.explanation: The verse states that the soul who eats any blood will be cut off from his people, consistent with the strict laws regarding blood consumption.

hard.title: Leviticus Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Leviticus Chapter 7.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 7, what shall happen to any soul that eats any manner of blood?
options: They shall be blessed
They shall be cut off from their people
They shall receive forgiveness
They shall be healed
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be cut off from their people
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:27 states that any soul who eats any manner of blood shall be cut off from his people, emphasizing the severity of this prohibition.

questions.question: Who is commanded to bring the offerings of the LORD made by fire, including the fat with the breast, as a wave offering before the LORD?
options: The Levites
The children of Israel
The high priest only
The priests' assistants
questions.correctAnswer: The children of Israel
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:29-30 commands the children of Israel to bring the offerings of the LORD made by fire with their own hands, including the fat with the breast as a wave offering.

questions.question: What is the portion given to Aaron and his sons from the peace offerings, according to Leviticus 7?
options: The entire breast and left shoulder
The wave breast and heave shoulder
Only the fat and kidneys
The rump and caul
questions.correctAnswer: The wave breast and heave shoulder
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:34 states that the wave breast and heave shoulder have been taken from the children of Israel's peace offerings and given to Aaron and his sons by statute forever.

questions.question: What will happen to a soul who eats the flesh of peace offerings while having uncleanness upon them?
options: They will be forgiven
They shall be cut off from their people
They will be blessed with prosperity
They will be offered another sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be cut off from their people
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:20 explains that anyone who eats the flesh of peace offerings with uncleanness upon them shall be cut off from their people, indicating a severe penalty for ritual impurity.

questions.question: Which part of the peace offering does the priest burn upon the altar, according to Leviticus 7?
options: The breast
The right shoulder
The fat
The kidneys
questions.correctAnswer: The fat
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:31 states that the priest shall burn the fat upon the altar, while the breast is given to Aaron and his sons.

questions.question: True or False: The remainder of the flesh of peace offerings can be eaten on the third day without consequence.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:18 states that eating the flesh of peace offerings on the third day is an abomination and the soul who eats it shall bear iniquity, so it is not allowed.

questions.question: What is forbidden to be eaten, whether from ox, sheep, or goat, according to the LORD's command in Leviticus 7?
options: The skin
The fat
The meat
The bones
questions.correctAnswer: The fat
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:23 commands that no manner of fat of ox, sheep, or goat shall be eaten, showing the sacredness of fat in offerings.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'wave offering' and 'heave offering' mentioned in Leviticus 7, in relation to priestly rights?
options: They were symbolic gifts to the Levites only
They were given to Aaron and his sons as a perpetual statute
They were burnt entirely on the altar
They were returned to the offerer
questions.correctAnswer: They were given to Aaron and his sons as a perpetual statute
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:34-36 explains that the wave breast and heave shoulder were taken from the children of Israel's peace offerings and given to Aaron and his sons by statute forever, signifying their priestly inheritance.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 7, what must be done if the flesh of the peace offering touches any unclean thing?
options: It shall be eaten by the priests only
It shall be burnt with fire
It shall be washed and then eaten
It shall be discarded outside the camp
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be burnt with fire
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:19 states that the flesh that touches any unclean thing shall not be eaten but shall be burnt with fire, emphasizing ritual purity.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of not eating blood as commanded in Leviticus 7:26-27?
options: Acts 15:20
Genesis 9:4
Deuteronomy 12:16
All of the above
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: The prohibition against eating blood in Leviticus 7:26-27 is echoed in Genesis 9:4, Deuteronomy 12:16, and reiterated in Acts 15:20, showing continuity in biblical dietary laws.

questions.question: What Hebrew word is translated as 'heave offering' in Leviticus 7, and what is its significance?
options: Terumah, meaning 'offering lifted up'
Minchah, meaning 'gift'
Zebach, meaning 'sacrifice'
Olah, meaning 'burnt offering'
questions.correctAnswer: Terumah, meaning 'offering lifted up'
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Terumah' used for 'heave offering' signifies an 'offering lifted up,' symbolizing the dedication of a portion to God and the priests, as seen in Leviticus 7:32-34.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 7:37-38 serve as an inclusio (literary device) in the chapter?
options: By summarizing the laws given earlier in the chapter
By introducing a new topic
By repeating the same phrase twice
By listing only the peace offerings
questions.correctAnswer: By summarizing the laws given earlier in the chapter
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:37-38 functions as an inclusio by summarizing the laws of various offerings given throughout the chapter, framing the entire section and reinforcing the covenant instructions.

questions.question: What consequence is given for a soul that eats the flesh of peace offerings after touching any unclean thing, according to Leviticus 7?
options: They shall be healed
They shall be cut off from their people
They shall be fined
They shall offer another sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be cut off from their people
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:21 states that anyone who touches any unclean thing and eats the flesh of peace offerings shall be cut off from his people, emphasizing the importance of purity.

questions.question: True or False: The priests are allowed to eat all the meat offerings baked, fried, or dressed in pans according to Leviticus 7.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:9 states that all the meat offering baked, fried, or dressed in pans shall be the priest's that offers it, showing their entitlement to these offerings.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 7, what must happen to the remainder of the flesh of a vow or voluntary offering if not eaten on the day it is offered?
options: It must be eaten the next day
It must be burned on the third day
It must be given to the Levites
It must be donated to the poor
questions.correctAnswer: It must be burned on the third day
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:16-17 instructs that the remainder of vow or voluntary offerings must be eaten on the day offered and the next day; any remainder on the third day must be burned with fire.

theological.title: Leviticus Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Leviticus Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 7:1 teach about the nature of the trespass offering?
options: It is most holy
It is common and ordinary
It is only for priests
It is optional for the people
questions.correctAnswer: It is most holy
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:1 explicitly states that the law of the trespass offering is 'most holy,' indicating its sacred and set-apart status.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 7:3, which parts of the animal are to be offered as fat in the trespass offering?
options: The rump and the fat covering the inward parts
Only the liver and kidneys
The head and feet
The skin and bones
questions.correctAnswer: The rump and the fat covering the inward parts
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:3 instructs the offerer to present all the fat including the rump and the fat that covereth the inwards, signifying the best parts dedicated to God.

questions.question: What is the prescribed use of the kidneys and the caul in the trespass offering, according to Leviticus 7:4?
options: They shall be taken away and burned on the altar
They shall be eaten by the priests
They shall be given to the poor
They shall be buried outside the camp
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be taken away and burned on the altar
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:4 commands that the kidneys and the fat on them, including the caul above the liver, be taken away to be burned, emphasizing the sanctity of the fat offerings.

questions.question: Leviticus 7:6 states that every male among the priests shall eat of the trespass offering. What does this indicate about the nature of the offering?
options: It is most holy and to be eaten in the holy place
It is common food for the people
It is forbidden to be eaten by anyone
It is only for the offerer
questions.correctAnswer: It is most holy and to be eaten in the holy place
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:6 shows the trespass offering is 'most holy' and restricted to priests, to be eaten in the holy place, highlighting the sanctity and priestly privilege.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 7:8, what part of the burnt offering does the priest keep for himself?
options: The skin of the burnt offering
The fat of the burnt offering
The blood of the burnt offering
The meat of the burnt offering
questions.correctAnswer: The skin of the burnt offering
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:8 clearly states that the priest who offers a burnt offering keeps the skin for himself, signifying a provision for the priestly family.

questions.question: What is the significance of the peace offering being eaten the same day it is offered, as commanded in Leviticus 7:15?
options: To prevent the offering from becoming unclean or unacceptable
To allow it to ferment and be shared
To save it for the next day’s meal
To donate leftovers to the poor
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent the offering from becoming unclean or unacceptable
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:15 commands that the flesh of peace offerings for thanksgiving be eaten the same day to avoid defilement or rejection, emphasizing ritual purity.

questions.question: Leviticus 7:18 warns that eating the flesh of a peace offering on the third day results in what consequence?
options: It shall not be accepted and the eater bears iniquity
It is considered a greater sacrifice
It is allowed with a sin offering
It is a sign of greater devotion
questions.correctAnswer: It shall not be accepted and the eater bears iniquity
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:18 states that if anyone eats the peace offering’s flesh on the third day, it is an abomination and the soul bears its iniquity, showing the seriousness of obedience.

questions.question: What doctrinal principle about holiness and cleanliness is taught by Leviticus 7:20-21 regarding those who eat peace offerings with uncleanness?
options: The person shall be cut off from his people
The person shall be forgiven without penalty
The person shall offer another sacrifice immediately
The person shall be restored after washing
questions.correctAnswer: The person shall be cut off from his people
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:20-21 teaches that eating the peace offering while unclean results in being cut off from the people, underscoring the gravity of holiness in worship.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 7:23 reveal about God's holiness in relation to eating animal fat?
options: God prohibits eating any fat of ox, sheep, or goat
God allows fat to be eaten freely
Fat may only be eaten by the priests
Fat must be burned outside the camp
questions.correctAnswer: God prohibits eating any fat of ox, sheep, or goat
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:23 commands the Israelites not to eat any fat from ox, sheep, or goat, reflecting God's standard of holiness and separation in diet.

questions.question: How do Leviticus 7:26-27 emphasize the sanctity of life and God's authority over it?
options: By forbidding the eating of any blood under penalty of being cut off
By permitting blood to be consumed in moderation
By requiring blood to be sprinkled on the altar only
By allowing blood only in meat offerings
questions.correctAnswer: By forbidding the eating of any blood under penalty of being cut off
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:26-27 prohibit eating blood, declaring that anyone who does shall be cut off, highlighting God's sovereignty over life represented by blood.

questions.question: What combined theological teaching do Leviticus 7:30-31 and 7:32-34 convey about the priestly portions from peace offerings?
options: The breast and right shoulder are given to priests by divine statute forever
The priests receive no part of the peace offerings
The entire sacrifice is consumed by the offerer
The portions are to be donated to the poor
questions.correctAnswer: The breast and right shoulder are given to priests by divine statute forever
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:30-31 and 7:32-34 together reveal that the breast and right shoulder are priestly portions given permanently by statute, signifying God's provision for the priesthood.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about God's justice and holiness is drawn from combining Leviticus 7:25 and 7:27 concerning eating fat and blood?
options: Eating fat or blood from sacrifices results in being cut off, showing the holiness and justice of God
Eating fat and blood is encouraged for sanctification
Fat and blood are irrelevant to God's holiness
Only the fat is prohibited, blood is allowed
questions.correctAnswer: Eating fat or blood from sacrifices results in being cut off, showing the holiness and justice of God
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:25 and 7:27 both state that eating fat or blood from sacrifices causes the person to be cut off, illustrating God's just and holy nature requiring strict obedience.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the detailed sacrificial laws in Leviticus 7 are merely archaic rituals with no spiritual significance. What does Leviticus 7 actually teach about the role of these offerings in God's redemptive plan?
options: They demonstrate God's holiness, the necessity of atonement, and foreshadow Christ's perfect sacrifice
They are arbitrary rules without meaning
They are only cultural practices irrelevant today
They promote human effort over divine grace
questions.correctAnswer: They demonstrate God's holiness, the necessity of atonement, and foreshadow Christ's perfect sacrifice
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7 teaches that sacrifices are 'most holy' (v.1), require the priest to make atonement (v.7), and involve offerings for sin and trespass, pointing to the need for a perfect atoning sacrifice fulfilled in Christ (see Hebrews 9:12).

questions.question: How does the combined teaching of Leviticus 7:11-14 and 7:36 contribute to understanding God's covenant faithfulness in worship?
options: They establish permanent statutes for offerings and priestly portions, showing God’s enduring covenant
They allow for flexible worship practices
They emphasize human merit over divine grace
They suggest offerings are temporary and optional
questions.correctAnswer: They establish permanent statutes for offerings and priestly portions, showing God’s enduring covenant
questions.explanation: Leviticus 7:11-14 outlines laws for peace offerings including offerings to the LORD and priestly portions; verse 36 confirms these statutes are eternal, demonstrating God's faithful covenantal requirements.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is particularly emphasized in Leviticus 7:22-23 where God commands not to eat any fat of ox, sheep, or goat?
options: God's holiness and demand for purity
God's mercy and forgiveness
God's omnipotence in creation
God's patience with sin
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and demand for purity
questions.explanation: In Leviticus 7:22-23, God’s command forbidding the eating of fat emphasizes His holiness and the call for the people to maintain ritual purity in accordance with His nature.
